description: Each media type's rate is its total Bytes divided by its total Milliseconds.

b.request: For tracks with a matching media type, calculate each media type’s rate as SUM(Bytes) / SUM(Milliseconds) and count its tracks; return the media type’s name, rate, track count, and rate minus the unweighted average of all media types’ rates only when its rate exceeds that average, without rounding
b.sql: WITH media_rates AS (SELECT m.Name AS media_type_name, CAST(SUM(t.Bytes) AS REAL) / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track AS t JOIN MediaType AS m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS average_rate FROM media_rates) SELECT r.media_type_name, r.rate, r.track_count, r.rate - o.average_rate AS rate_difference FROM media_rates AS r CROSS JOIN overall AS o WHERE r.rate > o.average_rate

c.request: Looking only at tracks that have a matching media type, what is each media type's bytes-per-millisecond rate (`Bytes` vs `Milliseconds`), and how many tracks does it have? Show only the media types whose rate is above the simple average of all media types' rates (each type counted once). For those, give the name, the rate, the track count, and how far the rate is above that average. Don't round anything. Each media type's rate is its total Bytes divided by its total Milliseconds.
c.sql: WITH media_rates AS (SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name, COUNT(*) AS track_count, 1.0 * SUM(t.Bytes) / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate FROM Track AS t JOIN MediaType AS m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name), average_rate AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS rate FROM media_rates) SELECT mr.Name, mr.rate, mr.track_count, mr.rate - ar.rate AS above_average FROM media_rates AS mr CROSS JOIN average_rate AS ar WHERE mr.rate > ar.rate

a.request: Match each track to its media type, dropping tracks without a match. For each media type name, work out a rate by adding up the `Bytes` of all its tracks and dividing that total by the sum of all its tracks' `Milliseconds` (one ratio of totals, not an average of per-track ratios), and count its tracks. Show only the media types whose rate is above the simple mean of all media types' rates (each type counted once). For those, show the name, the rate, the track count, and the rate minus that mean, all unrounded.
a.sql: WITH media_rates AS (SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name, 1.0 * SUM(t.Bytes) / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track AS t INNER JOIN MediaType AS m ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name), mean_rate AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS rate FROM media_rates) SELECT mr.Name, mr.rate, mr.track_count, mr.rate - mean_rate.rate AS rate_above_mean FROM media_rates AS mr CROSS JOIN mean_rate WHERE mr.rate > mean_rate.rate

d.request: Looking only at tracks with a matching media type, calculate each media type’s rate as its total `Bytes` divided by its total `Milliseconds`, and count its tracks. Find the simple average of those rates, counting each media type once. Show only media types whose rate exceeds that average, with each type’s name, rate, track count, and amount above the average. Do not round any values.
d.sql: WITH media_rates AS (SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name, 1.0 * SUM(t.Bytes) / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM MediaType AS m JOIN Track AS t ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name), average_rate AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS rate FROM media_rates) SELECT mr.Name AS name, mr.rate, mr.track_count, mr.rate - ar.rate AS amount_above_average FROM media_rates AS mr CROSS JOIN average_rate AS ar WHERE mr.rate > ar.rate
